title: I’m building arcade games controlled by hitting a real golf ball. Would love some feedback
author: Rocktato
selftext:
I’ve been working on Shanktuary Arcade: Pub Night, a collection of darts, beer pong, shuffleboard, billiards and bowling games with an unusual controller: a real golf ball.

For anyone unfamiliar with golf simulators, you hit a ball into a net or impact screen, and a device called a launch monitor measures the shot. My game uses that shot data, including ball speed and direction, to control the action on screen.

So beer pong and darts uses short chip shots, while shuffleboard, billiards and bowling use a putter. For games like billiards, you can adjust your aim with the keyboard, but the direction and speed of your actual putt still affect the shot.

I made an earlier version of these minigames with much simpler graphics. This trailer shows where the project is today. It’s still in development, and I’d love some outside opinions.

Do the games look fun and easy to understand? What would you change about the visuals, camera angles or how the gameplay is presented?
